chunks.heading: Copilot works with you. And you already have it.

blocks.x: Artificial intelligence is already part of our work environment at SAVI.
With Microsoft 365 Copilot you can find information, summarize conversations, prepare documents, analyze data and make better use of your meetings, using the tools you already know.
**You don’t need to be an AI expert. You just need to know where to start.**

It is an artificial intelligence assistant built into Microsoft 365 applications and also available from its own app. It can work with the context of your professional environment: emails, meetings, conversations and documents you have access to, depending on the enabled sources and features.

chunks.heading: What can you do with it?

blocks.x:
**Find information.** Locate conversations, decisions and documents related to your projects.
*Example:* “What did we agree with this client about the next campaign?”

**Get more from your meetings.** In Teams you can transcribe meetings when authorized; Copilot can use the available information to summarize topics, identify decisions, organize pending items and prepare follow-up emails.
*Example:* “Summarize this sales meeting; identify agreements and owners, and draft a follow-up.”

**Summarize what matters.** Turn long emails, conversations and documents into clear summaries.
*Example:* “Summarize this thread and highlight the open items.”

**Prepare content.** Create drafts of emails, documents, proposals and presentations to review and personalize.
*Example:* “Prepare an update email about this campaign.”

**Analyze and explore.** Compare results, identify trends, research markets and discover potential opportunities.
*Example:* “Compare the participation results for these weeks.”

**Copilot app:** open [copilot.cloud.microsoft](https://copilot.cloud.microsoft/) with your SAVI work account; check that you can actually access it from the corporate environment. It may also be available as a desktop app.
**Inside the apps:** Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and other Microsoft 365 tools include Copilot experiences. You can ask for help while you work.
Can’t see Copilot? Make sure you are signed in with your work account and contact IT if it still does not appear.

chunks.heading: How does it connect with your work?

items: **Microsoft 365:** Outlook emails, Teams meetings and conversations, OneDrive and SharePoint files, depending on access and features.
**Internet:** public information for research, when the tool allows searching the web.
**What you provide:** documents, text, files and specific references.

blocks.x: **Important:** Copilot does not automatically access everything in SAVI. It respects corporate permissions, but it does not fix misconfigured permissions. With our current setup, you should not assume that Salesforce, Jira or Offer Manager are automatically connected.

AI can speed up tasks, but it can also make mistakes, omit information or misinterpret a piece of data. Before using an answer with a client or making a decision, check the sources and review the results.
**Copilot does not replace your experience or professional judgment. It complements them.**

intro.heading: The best results start with good instructions

blocks.x: You don’t need to know hundreds of prompts. What matters is to explain what you want, provide context and verify the answer.

subs.name: How to write a good prompt

items: **Goal:** what you want to achieve.
**Context:** client, project, period and recipient.
**Sources:** which email, meeting, document or set of files to use.
**Instructions:** what to identify, prioritize and avoid.
**Format:** table, summary, list, email, presentation.
**Verification:** citations, distinction between facts and hypotheses, and information gaps.

blocks.x: Not every prompt needs every element.
**Not specific enough:** “Summarize this meeting.”

I need to prepare the follow-up for this sales meeting with [client]. Use the accessible transcript and identify confirmed agreements, tasks, owners and dates. Return a table. Separate decisions from open proposals. If there is no owner or date, write “Not specified”. Cite references when available.
blocks.title: Improved

subs.name: Don’t settle for the first answer

blocks.x: Use Copilot conversationally: summarize, ask for more depth, challenge hypotheses and turn the result into a deliverable.
**Sales iteration example:**

items: “Summarize the conclusions of this meeting.”
“Now identify pain points and needs we should investigate.”
“Separate confirmed needs from hypotheses and suggest five questions.”
“Turn the verified conclusions into a briefing for my team.”

blocks.x: **Useful phrases:** “Cite the source”, “Separate facts from recommendations”, “If information is missing, say so”, “Identify contradictions”, “Do not invent figures or commitments”, “Explain the calculation to me”, “What might I be overlooking?”. These phrases **reduce risks; they do not guarantee accuracy**.

Microsoft 365 Copilot includes enterprise data protection. Microsoft states that prompts, responses and associated corporate information are not used to train the foundation models. **This is not the same as having no records**: interactions may be subject to audit, retention and corporate controls.
Copilot respects Microsoft 365 permissions, but it does not fix documents that have been shared too broadly. You must follow SAVI’s confidentiality and privacy policies.
Indicative traffic light — PENDING VALIDATION BY IT/DPO

**Green:** ordinary work information for which processing is authorized.
**Amber:** confidential commercial, financial or contractual information, or consumers’ personal data; use only for an authorized purpose, with minimization and controls.
**Red:** passwords, credentials and any unauthorized information or processing; do not enter excessive data or disclose third-party information.

**Mandatory notice:** this traffic light is a provisional training guide, **not an approved corporate policy**. Until IT/DPO validate it, do not present it as an official rule or suggest that every “green” document is automatically authorized.
**Sharing results:** before distributing a document or report, check that it does not contain information about other clients, projects or people who are not among the recipients.

**Invention:** adds something not supported by the source.
**Omission:** leaves out a relevant exception or condition.
**Inference as fact:** turns a possible explanation into a confirmed statement.
**Check:** original sources, figures and formulas, validity, owners, recipients, conditions and the difference between facts and hypotheses. The greater the impact, the more human review is needed.
**SAVI method:** **Ask → Review → Open sources → Adjust → Use**.
